Three years ago I bought a standing desk because every article I read said sitting was killing me. Last month I lowered it to sitting height for good, and I want to write down why before I forget the details.

The first problem was that I never found a standing height that suited both typing and reading. At typing height the monitor was too low, and at reading height my wrists bent back on the keyboard. A monitor arm fixed part of it, but every adjustment moved something else out of place.

The second problem was my feet. I tried a mat, then a different mat, then shoes indoors, and by mid-afternoon my heels still ached. I started perching on a stool, which meant I was sitting anyway, just badly.

What actually helped was not the desk at all. A timer that goes off every forty minutes, a walk to the end of the garden and back, and a second chair by the window for reading on paper did more for my back than three years of standing.

I am not telling anyone to sell their desk. I am saying that moving often matters more than which way up you are while you are still.
